summary: Amalananda Ghosh was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at University College London (~1937–1938). He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1937–1968) and later as a Fellow at the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1968–1971).
Amalia Pezzali is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. She studied under Olivier Lacombe, Michel Hulin, and completed doctoral studies under T. R. V. Murti.

Amanda K. Goodman works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She earned her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under Robert H. Sharf, Luis Oscar Gómez, and Donald S. Lopez Jr., and holds a teaching position at the University of Toronto.
Amar Nath Pandeya is a scholar in the fields of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at the University of Delhi (attested 1968) and Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith (attested 1987).

Amar Singh is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He completed his doctorate under Anthony Kennedy Warder (attested 1984) and was taught by Rahul Sankrityayan (1960–1963), Bimal Krishna Matilal, and others.

Amara Ali is a linguist and Indologist. In posts attested in 2026, she serves as an Urdu lecturer at both the University of California, Berkeley and the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

Amaranatha Jha studied at Muir Central College (~1913–1917), where he became Professor of English in 1917. He later served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Allahabad (~1938–1946) and Banaras Hindu University (~1947–1948).
Amarasvar Thakur was an Indology scholar who held a post at the University of Calcutta (attested 1936) and served as General Editor for the Calcutta Sanskrit Series.

Amartya Sen is a philosopher and economist who studied at the University of Calcutta and the University of Cambridge. He held posts at the University of Delhi and the London School of Economics, and became a professor at Harvard University in ~2004.

Amaury de Riencourt was a scholar of history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Indology. He completed an MA at the University of Algiers (~1939–1940) and also studied at the Sorbonne and the University of Paris.
Amba Kulkarni works in computational linguistics and Indology. She earned her PhD from the University of Hyderabad by 2009 and holds a professorship there (attested 2018–2026).

Amber D. Carpenter specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under mentors including M. M. McCabe and Verity Harte. Her appointments include posts at the University of St Andrews, the University of York, and Yale-NUS College as associate professor.

Indologist Ambrogio Ballini studied at Bologna under Francesco Lorenzo Pullè and Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He held Sanskrit professorships at the University of Padua (1913), Università Cattolica del Sacro Cuore (1924), and Sapienza University of Rome (1941–1949).

Amelia Bonea is a historian and Indologist who studied at the University of Tokyo and Heidelberg University (PhD 2008–2012). She held posts at Oxford and Heidelberg before becoming Senior Lecturer at the University of Manchester (~2021).

Amelia Hall specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies and completed her doctorate at the University of Oxford by 2012. Her positions include Assistant Professor of Indo-Tibetan Buddhism at Naropa University (attested 2019).
Ameneh Shirazinejad is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She has held posts as an Arabic language tutor at George Washington University and as a Visiting Fellow at the University of Delhi.

Amin Sweeney was a scholar of linguistics who completed his doctorate at the University of London (~1967–1970). He taught at the National University of Malaysia (1970–1977) and the University of California, Berkeley, serving as department chair from 1986 to 1991.
Amita Chatterjee is a scholar of philosophy and Indology who served as a professor of philosophy at Jadavpur University (attested 1999 and 2009).
Amod Jayant Lele is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University under the supervision of Parimal G. Patil.

Amrit Madhav Ghatage was an Indologist and linguist. He served as Professor and Head of Linguistics at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1961–1978) and later as Vice-President of the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~1993–2003).
